title: Rapid cluster sampling of three-colourings on the square torus
formal: Do there exist C,c>0 such that WSK dynamics on proper three-colorings of every even square torus of side N≥4 satisfies t_mix(1/4)≤C N^c?
definitions: For integer N≥3, the square torus has vertices (Z/NZ)^2 and an undirected edge between vertices differing by 1 or −1 in exactly one coordinate and agreeing in the other; duplicate edges are suppressed. Here N is even and q=3. A state is a proper vertex coloring σ:V→{1,…,q}, meaning adjacent vertices have distinct colors. At each step choose an unordered pair of distinct colors uniformly from all q(q−1)/2 pairs. Form the subgraph induced by vertices having either color. Independently for each connected component, swap its two colors with probability 1/2 and otherwise retain them. The target μ is the uniform distribution over all proper colorings. For a finite-state transition matrix P with target distribution μ, define t_mix(1/4)=min{t∈N: max_x (1/2)∑_y |P^t(x,y)−μ(y)|≤1/4}, with value infinity if no such t exists. One step means the entire stated update, not one vertex recoloring. Even side length makes the graph bipartite and proper three-colorings nonempty. The target is mixing from every proper coloring to the uniform law on all such colorings. It therefore includes the required connectivity of the transition graph; restricting to a favorable sector is not allowed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation for the specified model.
context: The 2026 paper explicitly highlights the even periodic square lattice as a remaining WSK mixing question. Numerical evidence for a stronger constant-time claim is not a rigorous bound.
why: This tests whether cluster sampling remains efficient at a canonical antiferromagnetic critical point.

This would rigorously explain the sampler’s effectiveness at the critical antiferromagnetic point.

sentences: The graph is an even-sided periodic square grid.
Its states are all proper three-colorings.
Each step independently swaps components of a random color pair.
The question allows any fixed polynomial in the grid side length.
A proof must cover all initial colorings, not a selected communicating class.
